title: Uffington White Horse and St George's Dragon Mound

tellings.quote: mound right next to the Uffington white horse known as St. George and the Dragon's Mound, which is the spot where St. George slayed the dragon, right?

plain: Geoffrey Drumm, a man who talks about the purpose of ancient monuments, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Uffington in England, where a huge figure of a horse is cut into a hillside. He says a mound right next to it is known as St. George and the Dragon's Mound, the spot where, in legend, St. George killed the dragon. He raises it because it would tie the old dragon legend to that ancient site.
